To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the majority of MEDLINE users are physicians, that they use the system to find articles on a specific disease or condition, that they are not well trained in MEDLINE use, and that there is no one way to reach all potential users and nonusers.
MEDLINE end-users are not the same as MEDLINE subscribers and that the end-user is a very broad category.

MEDLINE is a valuable resource for health professionals and librarians; MEDLINE is a complex system; MEDLINE end-users are not well informed about MEDLINE; and MEDLINE end-users need more information about MEDLINE.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the information needs of end-users of a large bibliographic database.
the development of a new method for the study of the information needs in the medical field, and with the evaluation of the results of a survey of the information needs carried out in Italy.
how to reach and educate potential end-users of MEDLINE and to determine how best to do so.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MEDLINE users are a diverse group of people with different information needs.
the MEDLINE end-user community needs to be educated in the use of MEDLINE.
MEDLINE end-user education is an important and necessary part of the overall MEDLINE program and should be a high priority for the National Library of Medicine (NLM).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MEDLINE users are not a well-defined group and that the best method to educate them is to use the media.
the working group concluded that the MEDLINE user is the end-user, and that the user is not the librarian or the information specialist.

there is a need for an information service that will provide users of MEDLINE with the necessary tools to access the literature.
